# Beagle v0.24.0

Beagle v0.24.0 makes macro expansion structurally hygienic, adds a typed
structural matcher for authoring macros, and turns the full compiler gate into
a bounded parallel release preflight. The Racket compiler and checked-in
self-hosted compiler carry the same macro and identity contracts.

## Language and compiler

- **Macro hygiene now follows lexical scope identity end to end.** Binding and
  reference edges are resolved before lowering, preserved through source facts
  and hosted emitters, and serialized through the self-hosted compiler. Local
  shadowing, nested expansion, and intentional capture therefore retain the
  identity chosen at the macro boundary instead of depending on rewritten
  spellings.
- **Stable lexical identities survive layout-only source changes.** Scope and
  reference identities derive from structural provenance rather than transient
  names, so formatting or unrelated source movement does not silently remint
  the branch-corpus identity oracle.
- **Macros can use `syntax-match` for structural dispatch.** Patterns can
  distinguish identifiers and literals, match list, vector, and map shape,
  capture a final tail, and select clauses in source order. Invalid categories
  and malformed tail patterns report at the pattern span, while successful
  expansions continue through normal type checking.
- **The self-hosted compiler implements the same matcher.** The checked-in seed
  mirrors structural `syntax-match`, typed constant expansion, reachable branch
  checking, and malformed-pattern diagnostics, including a fixture that gates
  oracle and self-host agreement.

## Test infrastructure and performance

- **The full release tier runs as supervised parallel shards.** Each setup phase
  and shard has an explicit deadline, completion receipt, retained failure log,
  and subtree reaping. Worker results merge deterministically into the existing
  active, demoted, and gated-tier verdict.
- **Cold work is balanced and shared instead of repeated.** Shard assignment is
  based on measured compiler-heavy costs; Wasm tests share canonical generated
  fixtures; and Native Core checkpoints reuse verified frozen programs before
  C17 materialization. The ordinary active loop remains separate from the full
  release preflight.
- **The parallel C17 checkpoint suite is advisory for this seal.** Three
  independent release-preflight failures came from cold-cache prerequisites or
  scheduling rather than candidate behavior; the bounded replay of the final
  failure passed and verified the published checkpoint. The suite still runs
  under its unchanged 90-second owner, but it must be requalified before a
  later release can promote it back to blocking status.

## Compatibility

This pre-1.0 minor release removes the legacy name-rewriting hygiene path.
Macros or tools that inferred binding identity from rewritten symbol spellings
must consume the compiler's structural binding and reference identities. The
new `syntax-match` form is additive.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/tompassarelli/beagle/compare/v0.23.0...v0.24.0
